cands.bio: Democratic candidate for Alabama House District 85 in 2026. He advanced from the canceled May 19 Democratic primary without appearing on the ballot. Incumbent Republican Rick Rehm defeated him in the general election. No other biographical details were found.

endorsements.text: Listed by Ballotpedia as receiving voter guide recommendations from Tabitha's List: Candidates You Can Trust, Unburdening The Ballot: Voting Made Easy, and Wiregrass Rebels Ballot Party (all Sway voting groups).

cands.gaps: We could not find where Aristotle Kirkland was born or raised, or when he came to Alabama. We found nothing about his work history, any offices he has held, or his education. He did not complete Ballotpedia's 2026 Candidate Connection survey, so we found no stated positions on data centers, development, taxes, immigration, guns, abortion, education, policing or other issues. We found no public statements or actions from him on these topics. We found no news coverage of controversies, foreign ties, or notable individual endorsements.

cands.bio: Rick Rehm is a Republican who has represented Alabama House District 85 since November 2022. He served four years in the U.S. Army, then worked as a civilian frontline controller and facility manager at Fort Rucker. He served on Republican Party executive committees.
cands.gaps: We found no documented votes, sponsored bills or official actions on data centers, homestead property tax, land ownership, growth and land protection, immigration or H-1B, police funding, abortion, or school choice and teacher pay. His campaign site speaks only in general terms about blocking tax increases, election audits and veteran leadership. He did not complete Ballotpedia's candidate survey in 2022 or 2026. We found no stated positions on data centers or development. We found no documented controversies, and Ballotpedia lists no endorsements for 2026. Where he was raised before moving to Alabama is not stated. The sponsored-legislation table on his Ballotpedia page was empty in the version we read.
